competencies.title: Compare candidate values
competencies.observable_behavior: Given two scalar values, identify which should replace the current candidate under a stated comparison rule.

misconceptions.description: Reverses greater-than and less-than update conditions.
evidence_signals: selects smaller value for running maximum

competencies.title: Maintain one running maximum
competencies.observable_behavior: Trace or implement a single-pass update that preserves the maximum value seen so far.

misconceptions.description: Treats the running candidate as local to one iteration instead of persistent state.

competencies.title: Distinguish index from value
competencies.observable_behavior: Given a sequence traversal, correctly distinguish an element value from its position and choose the one required by the task.

misconceptions.description: Uses loop position where the algorithm requires the element value.

competencies.title: Predict a state transition
competencies.observable_behavior: Given current algorithm state and the next input value, predict the complete next state before executing code.

misconceptions.description: Updates one state variable while omitting another required simultaneous consequence.
evidence_signals: predicts largest change but leaves second candidate stale

competencies.title: Maintain two ordered extrema candidates
competencies.observable_behavior: Maintain largest and second-largest candidate values across a stream while preserving their ordering relationship.

misconceptions.description: Overwrites second-largest without preserving the previous largest when a new maximum arrives.
evidence_signals: sets largest before copying old largest

misconceptions.description: Fails to distinguish distinct-value and duplicate-allowed variants.
evidence_signals: cannot state whether equal values qualify
uses equality behavior inconsistent with prompt

competencies.title: Explain the two-candidate invariant
competencies.observable_behavior: Explain what largest and second-largest mean after each processed prefix and why their order is preserved.

misconceptions.description: States only a final-output property instead of a prefix-preserved invariant.
evidence_signals: description applies only after loop ends
cannot explain why each update is safe

competencies.title: Apply correct update ordering
competencies.observable_behavior: When a new maximum is found, preserve the old maximum as the second candidate before replacing the maximum.

misconceptions.description: Updates largest first and then copies the new largest into second-largest.
evidence_signals: both candidates become equal after new maximum

competencies.title: Implement second-largest in one pass
competencies.observable_behavior: Independently implement and debug a one-pass second-largest solution whose candidate state and duplicate policy match the task specification.

misconceptions.description: Algorithmic state is correct in explanation but implementation introduces unrelated Python mistakes.
evidence_signals: trace/explanation passes while blank implementation fails
syntax or indentation error without state-model error
